market_scope: US-listed semiconductor and AI data center infrastructure stocks only

china_a_shares.reason: Excluded because filing comparability and source confidence are below the US-market screen threshold.

safe_harbor: Educational information only. Not financial advice. Prices can move materially around earnings.

quote_source.name: Official company releases, SEC filings, Reuters-derived coverage, Yahoo Finance, and public market snapshots
quote_source.note: September 3, 2026 regular closes are used for historical comparability. September 4 intraday indications are excluded from the recorded screen.

market_emotion.basis: AI demand and hyperscaler capital commitments remain exceptional, but SOXX is about 4.4% below August 27 and both Broadcom and Credo sold off after earnings beats because guidance or margins did not clear elevated expectations.

strict_scoring.score_formula: forward fundamental surprise + narrative and expectation shift + supply-chain moat and diffusion + valuation and reaction gap + financial quality and positioning risk + evidence integrity
strict_scoring.interpretation: The score is an ordinal research rank, not a calibrated probability, target return, or backtested alpha estimate.
hard_gates: fresh attributable filing or company evidence
no unresolved accounting or liquidity red flag
valuation and market reaction assessed against expectations
buy list may be empty when no candidate reaches 82

position_sizing_overlay.rule: Use the conviction rank only for selection. Size is reduced independently for volatility, portfolio correlation, crowding, customer concentration, liquidity, and earnings risk.
position_sizing_overlay.initial_size: No more than about one-quarter of intended exposure for current staged buys, and only when each stated price condition is met.
position_sizing_overlay.exit_rule: Review or exit when the guidance, demand, margin, cash-flow, customer, or supply-chain thesis breaks; do not rely on price stops alone.

AVGO.reason: Q3 beat, 221% AI semiconductor growth, $13.7B free cash flow, a $21.7B Q4 AI guide, and approximately $350B of fiscal 2027-2028 AI revenue visibility outweigh a small total-guide miss. The post-report decline creates the freshest reaction gap, but site timing, debt, and margin compression cap conviction.

NVDA.reason: The Q2 filing, $108B Q3 guide, Rubin production, and full-rack platform pass. Price recovery reduces the reaction gap, while the $366B formal commitment stack, $36B of AI-cloud agreements, guarantees, customer concentration, and China restrictions reduce the risk score.

MU.reason: Q3 revenue grew 346%, GAAP gross margin reached 84.6%, free cash flow was $18.3B, and the $50B Q4 guide materially exceeded the prior bar. A roughly 6.7x forward multiple creates a large earnings-to-valuation gap, while memory cyclicality, $27B of net capex, and September 30 event risk cap position size.

KLAC.reason: Process-control intensity, double-digit growth, strong free cash flow, and a roughly 5.9% decline since August 27 create a cleaner equipment underreaction setup.

LRCX.reason: Revenue and earnings growth are excellent and the pullback improved valuation, but broad equipment order activity remains cool and the setup ranks below KLAC.

AMAT.reason: Fiscal Q3 growth and DRAM exposure pass, but valuation, a weak price trend, and only modest broader equipment order improvement cap the score.

CRDO.reason: Revenue grew 114.7% and the forward valuation reset, but gross-margin compression, two customers representing 85% of receivables, $88.0M of stock compensation against $90.2M operating cash flow, and the 20% earnings-day break require a durable base.

FORM.reason: HBM and advanced-package test intensity drove a major earnings inflection, but semicap cyclicality, customer concentration, and price-base risk remain.

MRVL.reason: Revenue, data-center growth, and raised guidance pass, but the stock is still about 38x forward earnings and lacks a durable base. The new customer warrant for up to 59.0M shares at $206.58, customer concentration, acquisitions, and preferred-share conversion risk reduce per-share conviction.

PDFS.reason: Q2 passed the profit, backlog, and cash-flow gates, but valuation, integration, customer concentration, and older evidence prevent a current buy rating.

rankings.positioning: Quarter-size starter positions only. AVGO requires the $342-$357 post-report zone to hold; MU is preferred below $960 or on a $920-$940 retest with no chase above $1,000 before September 30; NVDA should be bought only on an orderly retest near $225; KLAC is preferred near $170-$173.
keep_caution_today: CRDO until margins, cash conversion, and its post-earnings base improve
MRVL until dilution-adjusted custom-silicon economics and a durable base improve
AMAT and LRCX until equipment breadth improves
FORM and PDFS for speculative sizing only

supply_chain_view.framework: Manufacturable silicon to complete powered site
next_two_year_bottlenecks: HBM and DRAM allocation plus HBM4 qualification
CoWoS, high-end substrates, hybrid bonding, package power integrity, yield, and inspection
800G and 1.6T networking, AECs, CPO, coherency, silicon photonics, and secure data movement

source_intelligence.signal: Broadcom and Credo both beat, but a small guide shortfall and margin compression failed elevated market expectations.
Package power integrity, liquid cooling, megawatt distribution, and local HBM packaging capacity are moving into the core architecture.
Accelerator economics link HBM, packaging yields, networking, site megawatts, cloud financing, and token-level returns.
Broadcom's call supports an approximately $350B two-year AI semiconductor outlook, with six customers and site readiness as a timing constraint.
Equipment order activity improved slightly but remains cool; DRAM and HBM are strengthening faster than NAND.
HBM, high-end substrates, CoWoS, and leading-edge nodes remain constrained; memory can exceed 75% of some AI-server bills of materials.
Record SEMICON Taiwan participation centers on advanced nodes, packaging, smart fabs, and chiplets; equipment and materials sales continue to grow.
Hot Chips systems show heterogeneous, rack-scale AI compute raising the value of coherency, scheduling, networking, power, and serviceability.
Optical networking funding and secure AI data-platform releases confirm that useful cluster output depends on data movement and operations.
Broadcom's strong quarter did not prevent a post-report decline when its total-revenue outlook missed a very high consensus bar.
Broadcom's mix-driven gross-margin compression and Credo's reset show why revenue growth must be checked against margin quality and valuation.
